title: Implement a Pluggable Data Enrichment Component with a Redis Backend
description: EduStream Nexus requires a new capability to enrich streaming data in real-time. This involves creating a new, generic 'enrichment' stage in the pipeline that can be used to augment events with data from external sources. The first implementation of this new component type will be a 'Redis Enricher', which looks up data in a Redis cache based on a key from the incoming event and adds the retrieved data back into the event. This task is designed to be completed over multiple development sessions, testing the agent's ability to retain context, manage complex changes across the codebase, and follow a structured development process.

project_spec.name: EduStream Nexus
project_spec.description:
EduStream Nexus is an expert-level, component-based data-streaming platform written in C that enables universities, online course providers, and research labs to ingest, transform, analyze, and visualize real-time learning telemetry at scale. From LMS clickstreams and virtual-lab sensor feeds to adaptive-quiz scores and remote-classroom video metrics, the system uses rigorously defined ETL and event-streaming components to guarantee data quality, provide low-latency insights to instructors, and fuel data-driven instructional design.

The platform’s architecture decomposes each educational data pipeline into interchangeable C shared-object components—Ingestion Adapters, Validation Filters, Transformation Strategies, Quality-Check Observers, Storage Sinks, Visualization Emitters, and Recovery Supervisors—wired together with a lightweight plug-in/contract mechanism. This separation lets institutions mix-and-match components (e.g., switch from Kafka to MQTT ingestion, or swap rule-based validation for ML-driven anomaly detection) without touching adjacent modules, thereby supporting the diverse and evolving data needs of modern education.
dependencies: librdkafka (C client for Apache Kafka) – high-throughput event streaming
libuv – asynchronous I/O and cross-platform scheduling
Apache Arrow C Flight – columnar in-memory data frames for batch/stream unification
Protobuf-C – efficient message serialization between microservices
SQLite/LibPQ (PostgreSQL C API) – pluggable relational storage and metadata catalog
Parquet-C – compressed columnar files for the Data Lake landing zone
OpenMPI – distributed parallel processing in transformation/batch components
Prometheus C Client – real-time monitoring and alerting hooks
jansson – fast JSON parsing for flexible schema validation
libzip + zstd – compressed archival of learning event batches
OpenSSL – encrypted transport for student-data privacy compliance
CUnit – unit/contract tests for component conformance
